extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, interested parties, patent practitioners and agents (including foreign-domiciled applicants) involved in Korean IPTAB proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official procedural and substantive standards governing ex parte appeals and inter partes trials before the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board (IPTAB), including who may file, time limits, types of trials, panel composition, and legal effects of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of IPTAB jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPTAB conducts and hears inter partes trials and ex parte appeals that involve IP rights, including patent, utility model, design, and trademark, and renders decisions thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPTAB is a quasi-judicial body within the Ministry of Intellectual Property providing independent review of adverse examiner decisions (ex parte appeals) and adjudicating disputes over validity of issued patents (inter partes trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of administrative remedies before judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: One must exhaust administrative remedies prior to seeking judicial review for IP-related cases; one can file a lawsuit before the Court only after he/she has decisions from the IPTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korea has a three-instance system for IP-related disputes; IPTAB serves as the first instance whose decisions can be appealed to the Patent Court and Supreme Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition for deciding cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In the majority of cases, a case is reviewed in a composition of 3 administrative judges, consisting of the chairperson, rapporteur and an additional member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A panel of judges shall deliberate regarding the decision to be taken. An expanded panel of 5 judges may hear and decide the case where appropriate, including cases involving issues that span a number of technical fields, cases with legal/technical difficulty and/or importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing deadline for ex parte appeals against examiner rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person has an objection to an examiner's decision to reject a patent application or to a decision to reject an application to register the extended term of a patent, he/she may file an appeal within 30 months from the date when he/she is served with a certified copy of the examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exception may be applied in cases where a person resides in an area that is remote or difficult to access; in such cases, the Minister of MOIP may extend the period to 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination request (post-July 1, 2009 applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a patent application filed on or after July 1, 2009, an applicant may request re-examination or file an appeal following an adverse decision made by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent applicant may file a request to re-examine his/her patent application after amending the specification or drawings of the patent application within 30 months after receipt of a certified copy of the decision to reject the patent application; however, an applicant is not allowed to request a re-examination once a petition for trial is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for Correction — permissible corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent holder may file a petition for trial to correct specifications or drawings in any of the following cases: to narrow a claim; to correct a clerical error; or to clarify an ambiguous description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial for correction is intended to protect a patent invention by providing an opportunity for a patentee to make corrections under the condition that there are no unexpected losses or damages caused to any third parties. However, this shall not apply when a patent opposition is pending before the IPTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effect when correction decision becomes final
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trial decision to correct specifications or drawings of a patented invention becomes final and conclusive, it shall be deemed that filing and laying open the relevant patent application, a decision or trial ruling to grant a patent, and the registration of the grant of the patent have been made according to the corrected specification or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the retroactive legal effect of an affirmed correction on the public record and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request a trial for invalidation (inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party or an examiner may request a trial to review the validity of an issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a patent containing two or more claims, a request for trial for invalidation may be made for each claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for patent invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for invalidation are generally the same as the grounds for rejection of a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links invalidation claims to the statutory/earlier examination grounds used during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and effect of invalidation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A trial for invalidation may be requested even after the expiration of the patent right. Where a trial decision to invalidate a patent becomes final and conclusive, the patent right shall be deemed never to have existed; however, where a patent is invalidated by any reason that arose after the granting of a patent, the patent right is deemed not to have existed from the time when such reason is originated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies retrospective and temporal effects of final invalidation rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial to Invalidate Registration for Extension of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party or examiner may request a trial to invalidate the registration of an extension of a patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific inter partes remedy targeted at extensions of patent term/registration of extended term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial to Confirm the Scope of Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee or an interested person may request a trial to confirm the scope of a patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a petition to confirm the scope of at least two claims in a patent, a petition may be filed for each claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial to Invalidate Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party or examiner may request a trial to invalidate corrections, where the specifications or drawings of a patented invention have been corrected in violation of Article 136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a decision to invalidate corrections of specifications or drawings becomes final and conclusive, the correction shall be deemed never to have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for Grant of Non-exclusive Licenses — eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee requires the use of the patent right of a prior patentee to operate his/her patented invention, or when a prior patentee refuses to grant permission to use the patent right without justifiable reasons, he/she may request a trial for grant of a non-exclusive license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make such a request, it is required that the patented invention of the later patentee should constitute a substantial technical advance in comparison with the patented invention or registered utility model of the prior patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for representation of foreign-domiciled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for a trial is made against a foreign-domiciled applicant (a person who has neither a domicile nor a place of business in the Republic of Korea), in accordance with the Patent Act Article 5, a foreign-domiciled applicant shall not initiate any patent-related procedure or file legal proceedings ... unless he/she is represented by a patent administrator (an agent with respect to his/her patent, who has a domicile or a place of business in the Republic of Korea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule exists because receiving copies of written requests and other documents can be problematic without a local patent administrator, potentially causing lapses of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on re-examination after filing a petition for trial
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not allowed to request a re-examination once a petition for trial is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural bar prevents simultaneous pursuit of re-examination and trial on the same application after a petition for trial has been initiated.
